query: What kinds of expenses tend to get declined, and does it differ by department?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, interpretable categories of what is being expensed (hardware, cloud, travel, etc.); a strong external axis to segment decline rates against.

per_column.name: asset_specificity
per_column.rationale: Named-model vs generic-category is an interpretable, well-balanced dimension that plausibly associates with declines and supports meaningful grouping.

per_column.name: expense_purpose_signal
per_column.rationale: Purpose of expense (routine refresh, maintenance, travel, new-employee) gives clear, comparable segments to cross with decline outcomes.

per_column.name: request_justification_clarity
per_column.rationale: Clarity of justification is an interpretable ordinal-ish segmentation that plausibly relates to approval/decline and can be grouped on.

per_column.name: high_value_indicator
per_column.rationale: A clean binary cost-tier flag; interpretable and a classic dimension to compare decline rates, though it partially derives from the existing amount column.

per_column.name: department_procurement_profile
per_column.rationale: Values are literally department names (customer_support, sales, it, ...), duplicating the existing department column rather than adding an external associational variable.

per_column.name: request_automation_indicator
per_column.rationale: Automated vs manual request is an interpretable, reasonably balanced binary segment that could plausibly correlate with decline outcomes.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are interpretable, well-separated categorical dimensions that open genuine associational axes around declines (asset type, specificity, purpose, justification clarity, value tier, automation), directly enabling exploration of what gets declined and cross-tabbing by segment. One column (department_procurement_profile) merely restates the existing department field and adds no new relationship, and high_value_indicator partly derives from amount. As a set they support discovering interpretable relationships with the focus reasonably well, but the redundancy prevents a top score.
